exercises.prompt: You are given requests, an array of Seattle 311 service-request records, each an object { type, neighborhood, daysOpen, status } — for example { type: 'Pothole', neighborhood: 'Ballard', daysOpen: 6, status: 'open' } (status is always 'open' or 'closed'). Implement countByNeighborhood(requests) so it returns an object mapping each neighborhood to how many requests it has — { neighborhood: count }. countByNeighborhood(requests) is {'Ballard': 3, 'Fremont': 4, 'Downtown': 3, 'Capitol Hill': 2, 'Georgetown': 3}. An empty array returns an empty object {}.
exercises.fixture:
const requests = [
  { type: 'Pothole', neighborhood: 'Ballard', daysOpen: 6, status: 'open' },
  { type: 'Pothole', neighborhood: 'Fremont', daysOpen: 8, status: 'closed' },
  { type: 'Pothole', neighborhood: 'Downtown', daysOpen: 50, status: 'open' },
  { type: 'Graffiti', neighborhood: 'Capitol Hill', daysOpen: 40, status: 'closed' },
  { type: 'Graffiti', neighborhood: 'Ballard', daysOpen: 18, status: 'open' },
  { type: 'Graffiti', neighborhood: 'Downtown', daysOpen: 30, status: 'closed' },
  { type: 'Streetlight', neighborhood: 'Fremont', daysOpen: 12, status: 'open' },
  { type: 'Streetlight', neighborhood: 'Georgetown', daysOpen: 20, status: 'open' },
  { type: 'Illegal Dumping', neighborhood: 'Georgetown', daysOpen: 25, status: 'open' },
  { type: 'Illegal Dumping', neighborhood: 'Ballard', daysOpen: 9, status: 'closed' },
  { type: 'Abandoned Vehicle', neighborhood: 'Capitol Hill', daysOpen: 44, status: 'closed' },
  { type: 'Abandoned Vehicle', neighborhood: 'Downtown', daysOpen: 10, status: 'open' },
  { type: 'Abandoned Vehicle', neighborhood: 'Fremont', daysOpen: 4, status: 'closed' },
  { type: 'Pothole', neighborhood: 'Georgetown', daysOpen: 15, status: 'open' },
  { type: 'Graffiti', neighborhood: 'Fremont', daysOpen: 16, status: 'closed' }
]

tests.expr: countByNeighborhood([{ type: 'a', neighborhood: 'Fremont', daysOpen: 1, status: 'open' }, { type: 'b', neighborhood: 'Fremont', daysOpen: 2, status: 'closed' }])

hints: This is a frequency tally keyed by each request's neighborhood field.
Walk the requests bumping counts[r.neighborhood] = (counts[r.neighborhood] || 0) + 1.
Loop the requests updating counts[r.neighborhood] = (counts[r.neighborhood] || 0) + 1, then return counts — an empty array never enters the loop and returns {}.

hints: Keep only the closed requests, then ask how many there are.
filter(r => r.status === 'closed') selects the closed ones, and .length counts them.
